findings.description: Valid single-line Python definitions such as `def f(): return 1` never satisfy the new signature termination condition because their lines do not end with a colon.
findings.failure_mode: The scan advances into subsequent definitions or beyond the supplied end, extending f's computed scope and incorrectly awarding recall credit for citations outside that function.
findings.suggested_fix: Identify the signature's terminating colon using Python tokenization, including definitions with an inline body, and bound the resulting scope to end.

findings.description: The presence of a statistics flag does not make a git diff stat-only. For example, `git diff --no-index --stat --patch pr/head/file file` prints both statistics and the complete patch.
findings.failure_mode: The unconditional continue drops actual patch exposure, allowing a transcript that displayed planted defects to receive an incorrect unexposed classification.
findings.suggested_fix: Account for patch-producing options and their ordering before classifying a git diff as stat-only.

findings.description: Fence state retains only the delimiter character, so a triple-backtick line incorrectly closes a block opened with four backticks. Such blocks commonly contain triple-backtick examples.
findings.failure_mode: Subsequent hash-prefixed code inside the still-open Markdown fence becomes a section heading, splitting the real section and incorrectly changing same-scope recall credit.
findings.suggested_fix: Track the opening delimiter length and accept a closing fence only when it uses the same character, has at least that length, and contains only trailing whitespace.

findings.description: `val` is normalized so a backslash-continued command becomes one logical line, but the fixture side `fl` (head/** lines and head.diff lines) is still indexed by physical line. A verbatim quotation of a backslash-continued fixture command such as `gh api repos/0xHoneyJar/loa/pulls \` + `  --jq '.[].title'` was exempt before (each physical line was a substring of a fixture line) and is now a repo_name hit, because the joined logical line (which also carries the continuation line's indentation as embedded spaces) is a substring of no single fixture line.
findings.failure_mode: Runs that copy a multi-line PR command verbatim are newly reported `contaminated.pattern=repo_name`; the diff's own doc comment says quoting PR content is not a probe.
findings.suggested_fix: Apply the same `\\\n` join (and whitespace normalization) when building `fl`, or test the unit against both the physical-line and logical-line forms before returning None.

findings.cross_file_justification: The sentinel's effect is decided by how evals/graders/recall-vs-defects.sh resolves its head directory and reads files under it; that fallback code is not in the diff and no test in this change covers a task without head/.
findings.description: EVAL_HEAD_DIR is set to `<grading>/.no-head` and only replaced when `resolve_pr_fixture(t)` succeeds and head/ is a directory. If recall-vs-defects.sh selects `${EVAL_HEAD_DIR:-$WS/pr/head}` the sentinel works, but every same-scope read then targets a missing tree and any unguarded open()/listdir aborts the whole recall grade. If it instead checks `-d` and falls back, the sentinel is a no-op and the sandbox copy is still read, so DISS-C-003 is not actually fixed. AG-52/53 and RG-40..42 cover C-001/2/4/5/6; nothing exercises the no-head path.
findings.failure_mode: Either recall grading errors for tasks whose fixture lacks head/ (previously they graded via the sandbox fallback), or the fix silently does nothing.
findings.suggested_fix: Have recall-vs-defects.sh treat a set-but-missing EVAL_HEAD_DIR explicitly: no fallback, no same-scope credit, no exception. Add a bats case with a task whose fixture has head.diff but no head/ and assert the grade completes with function-only credit absent.

findings.description: Any git command containing a DIFF_STAT_FLAGS word is skipped as stat-only. git prints the full patch after the summary when a patch flag is also present (`git diff --stat -p`, `--numstat --patch`, `--name-status -u`), so those commands expose content but are never recorded.
findings.failure_mode: A false negative in the oracle-exposure detector: a run that dumps the fixture diff with `--stat -p` is graded as not exposed.
findings.suggested_fix: Skip only when no `-p`, `-u`, `--patch`, `--patch-with-stat` or `--patch-with-raw` is also among `w` (git suppresses the patch by default when a stat flag is given, so that check is sufficient).

findings.description: `|&` (bash's shorthand for `2>&1 |`) still produces a spurious empty segment: the `|` is recorded as a pipe, then the `&` (previous char `|`, next char space) falls to the separator branch. `diff a b |& wc -l` becomes [diff…,"|"], ["",";"], ["wc -l",…]; in oracle_plan `nxt` for the diff segment is `[]`, silent_sink is never consulted, and the diff is reported exposed although nothing printed.
findings.failure_mode: False oracle exposure for the exact pattern (stderr merged then counted) that this hunk sets out to handle, when the agent uses the `|&` spelling.
findings.suggested_fix: In the `|` branch consume a following `&` as part of the pipe token, or add `cmd[i-1:i] == "|"` to the new redirection condition.

findings.description: The fence tracker closes on the first later line with the same fence character regardless of length, and accepts an opener whose remainder contains backticks. CommonMark requires the closer to be at least as long as the opener with no info string, and forbids backticks in a backtick fence's info string. A doc that shows a ``` example inside a ```` fence (the normal way to document markdown in .claude/docs) closes at the inner ``` and the example's `# ...` lines become headings again; a line beginning with an inline span like ```` ```foo``` ```` opens a fence that never closes, so every later heading in that file is dropped and preceding sections run to EOF.
findings.failure_mode: Same-scope credit misassigned: headings lost or spurious headings created in files with nested fences or leading inline code spans.
findings.suggested_fix: Record (char, length) on open; close only on `^\s{0,3}(char){length,}\s*$`; ignore backtick openers whose remainder contains a backtick.

findings.description: The signature scan has no exit when no line satisfies `depth <= 0 and endswith(':')`: a one-liner `def f(): return 1` / `def f(): ...` stub, or a signature with `(` or `#` inside a string default (`def parse(s, comment="#"):` strips the rest of the line and leaves depth 1), runs `j` to `end + 1`, so `last = end + 1` and the function returns a line past `end` (past the file when `end == len(lines)`). Before this change a one-liner's scope was [h, h]; now it spans every blank and comment line up to and including the next header's line.
findings.failure_mode: Over-wide scope for one-liner defs and for signatures containing string parens/hashes; a returned close line beyond the file if any caller indexes `lines[close - 1]`.
findings.suggested_fix: Fall back to `last = h` when the while loop exits without a break; stop the scan at the first line after h whose indentation is <= lv; strip `#` and count parens only outside string literals (or use `tokenize`).

findings.description: The manifest hash for smoke/review-r17/task.yaml is updated, but no change to that file appears in the diff and nothing else in this change refers to review-r17 (AG-53 uses review-r18). Either the fixture edit was not staged, in which case manifest verification fails against the committed file, or the fixture is untracked and the manifest now records an unreviewable local change.
findings.failure_mode: Manifest check fails for the smoke suite, or a fixture semantic change ships without review.
findings.suggested_fix: Include the task.yaml change in the same commit (or state why its hash moved) and run the manifest verification before merging.

findings.description: `-L` / `--files-without-match` prints only filenames but is not matched (the class is lowercase `[cql]`), and `egrep`, `fgrep` and `rg` with `-c`/`-l`/`-q` are not recognized. Only the immediately following pipe segment is consulted, so `diff a b | grep planted | wc -l` and `diff a b | sort >/dev/null` are still counted as exposure although nothing is printed.
findings.failure_mode: False oracle exposure for common two-stage pipelines; missed silence for grep -L and rg.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `L` and `--files-without-match`; include egrep/fgrep/rg; walk the pipeline to its last segment and treat the diff as silent when that sink is non-printing or carries a DEVNULL redirection.

findings.description: `printf 'for r in \\\\\n ...'` emits two backslashes before the newline (printf collapses `\\\\` to `\\`), which bash reads as an escaped backslash followed by a plain newline, not a line continuation. The grader still returns repo_name because the joined line `for r in \   0xHoneyJar/loa` matches no fixture line, so the case passes via the join path rather than the bare-token guard it is named for; only the heredoc case exercises that guard.
findings.failure_mode: The for-list continuation scenario from DISS-C-002 is not actually covered; a regression in the bare-token guard would still pass this assertion.
findings.suggested_fix: Use a single backslash (`\\\n`) in the printf format or a quoted heredoc, and assert on that case alone that `.contamination_exempt` is empty.
